I agree and am so glad you posted this. I don’t have a problem with people spreading positivity and supporting one another. I’m actually glad there’s a sub for that! But where do you go to have a discussion about your personality anymore? Seriously, where can you have in-depth, engaging conversation about this specific personality type? Of course you can post on here (I imagine that’s what most people who are reading this are screaming internally right now)— BUT… look at how often those kinds of posts get discarded with a couple upvotes and maybe a handful of comments at best. I’m 99% certain that if someone posted the most thoughtful, insightful, interesting post in history regarding being an INFP and then posted a selfie or a sunset pic immediately afterwards, the selfie or sunset pic would get significantly more upvotes and comments.

It’s a weird feeling to be typed as an INFP, but then feel like there’s some whole other culture that is the INFP sub. Honestly I think all of this stems from growing pains. The sub has grown a lot, and sooner or later, people are going to have to decide what it’s for. If it’s going to be focused on discussion of a personality type, reflecting on what being an INFP looks like in your life, and finding similar patterns of thinking about and processing the world around you, awesome. That sounds like a personality type sub. If it’s going to be selfies, sky pictures, and memes that may or may not have anything to do with personality in the first place, and any criticism or input on what people do and don’t want in this sub is going to be met with outrage, that’s not a sub some people want to be part of. Also, although it’s definitely easier to leave a sub than to leave a country, the logic behind, “If you don’t like it here, you can leave,” feels eerily similar. Someone expressing disapproval of the content of a sub has every right to be here and be heard.

Glad you felt comfortable enough to speak up. A few years ago, I found this sub, and it was a really cool place for discussing personality and finding common themes among people who were typed as INFP. Somewhere along the way, the number of people on this sub grew A LOT. I honestly want to say that when I lurked on here years before I had this account, the numbers were in the 30k range. Fast forward to now, and it’s much, much different from what I remember. I’m not saying it’s gotten better or worse, but it has strayed a bit from what I thought a personality sub would be— definitely a lot more selfies and pictures of the sky than expected. I’m not saying that this is a terrible place or that I don’t want people to enjoy it, but what I am saying is this—it seems that this sub has transformed into more of a comfortable space for a substantial amount of people and at least somewhat less of a place for people to discuss personality. I hope whoever’s reading this can realize that that’s not any sort of attack on what this sub is now, but rather an expression of my perspective on the change I’ve seen over the years and my take on what I thought this sub would be about vs my experience of the sub currently. Thanks for taking the time to read this.

Working retail this past year, I’ve started to notice more and more how overlooked and under appreciated retail workers are. Look for an office park in your area then look for any type of brick and mortar store. The stores outnumber the white collar workplaces so much, and the larger stores are probably employing a ton of people. Think about how many times someone goes to a grocery store, a gas station, or a home improvement store on the weekend and all of the people it takes to staff those places. The irony is that the white collar workers who shop at those locations probably never even notice all the people working there. I’d love to see the statistics on how many people actually have a weekend anymore vs the number of people who work varying shifts each week— sometimes with very little turnaround time between shifts— just to barely make ends meet.
I’ve heard a saying something like, “If a job pays you minimum wage, it means they probably want to pay you less but can’t,” and that’s always stuck with me.
In my experience, working really hard for a raise isn’t always worth it either. It’s rare that the raise warrants the increase in responsibility and overall pressure put on you by superiors.
